data.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek word 'Chrystos' meaning 'anointed'. In Christianity, the name 'Chrystos' is associated with Jesus Christ, who was anointed with oil during His baptism. The name 'Chrystelle' is a feminine variation of the name, meaning 'anointed one' or 'Christ bearer'. The name Chrystelle carries the meaning “Anointed with oil or Christ” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Chrystelle usually hope their child will grow to embody anointed with oil or christ and live with faith, good character and purpose.

in_hebrew.name: כריסטל
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם כריסטל הוא נגזר מהמילה היוונית 'Χρυστή' (כריסטי), שפירושה 'זהב' ו- 'אל', שפירושה 'אלוהים' או 'אלוה'. השם מתאר את המשיח כנזר זהב, או שמן המשחה. השימוש בשם זה הוא נדיר בקרב יהודים, אך הוא מוכר יותר בקרב נוצרים.

in_greek.name: Χρυστήλλω
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Χρυστήλλω προέρχεται από τις ελληνικές λέξεις 'χρυσή' (chrysí), που σημαίνει 'χρυσός' και 'Χρήστος' (Christos), που σημαίνει 'Αναζωογονημένος' ή 'Μεσσίας'. Στην Καινή Διαθήκη, ο Χρήστος αναφέρεται ως ο Υιός του Θεού. Το όνομα Χρυστήλλω είναι σύμβολο πίστης και πνευματικής αγάπης.

in_latin.name: Chrystella
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Chrystella derivatur ex verbis latinized Graecis 'χρυσός' (aureus) et 'Χρήστος' (Christus). Significat autem Unctum, seu Christum, qui est Unctio Dei. Nomen hoc est imago devotionis et spiritualis amoris.

in_english.name: Chrystelle

historical_references.reference: Saint Chrystelle, also known as Saint Christelle or Sainte Christelle, was a legendary French virgin and hermit. According to legend, she lived in the 5th century in a cave near the town of Villefranche-du-Périgord, in what is now southwestern France. She is said to have lived a solitary life in the forest, caring for the sick and the poor, and performing many miracles. Her cult is still celebrated in the region today.

Another reference to the name Chrystelle comes from a 19th century French novel called 'Narcisse' by Prosper Mérimée. In this novel, the protagonist, Narcisse, falls in love with a beautiful woman named Chrystelle, who is revealed to be a statue brought to life by a sorcerer. This name may have gained popularity as a result of the novel's influence.
